items.title: Comedy festival in Mississauga abruptly cancelled days before event
items.summary: A comedy festival that was expected to come to Mississauga this weekend has been abruptly cancelled. The Great Outdoors Comedy Festival was scheduled to take place at Erindale Park, located near the University of Toronto Mississauga, from Sept. 11 to 13. Several big names in comedy were billed for the weekend. Stavros Halkias, Fred Armisen, James Austin Johnson, and John Mulaney were slated to be Friday’s headliners. J. Miller, Jordan Jansen, and Brad Williams, while Ronny Chieng, Michael Kosta, and Hasan Minhaj were expected to wrap the festival up on Sunday. Festival organizers said in an online statement that they decided to postpone the upcoming event, but did not provide a clear reason why that decision was made. “We know there was a lot of excitement around the show, but our priority is to deliver the best possible festival, and we believe that postponing this week’s performance is the right decision to ensure we can do that,” the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival wrote. Organizers said they are exploring new dates and will contact festivalgoers as soon as they have one. “If you’ve purchased tickets, please stay tuned as we’ll be following up directly,” they wrote.

items.title: Massive festival cancelled just days before opening in southern Ontario
items.summary: A major outdoor comedy festival that was expected to bring thousands of people to Mississauga’s Erindale Park this weekend has been called off, just days before it was scheduled to begin. Ward 7 Councillor Dipika Damerla announced the news on social media Tuesday afternoon (Sept. 8), saying the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival would not proceed as planned. “We are sorry to share that the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival in Mississauga will not be happening as planned. After careful consideration, the team has made the difficult decision to postpone our show scheduled for September 11th-13th, 2026,” organizers said in a statement. “We know there was a lot of excitement around the show, but our priority is to deliver the best possible festival, and we believe that postponing this week’s performance is the right decision to ensure we can do that. We’re exploring new dates and will be back with an update as soon as we have one. ” The festival was to make its Mississauga debut at Erindale Park, with five shows featuring some of the biggest names in North American comedy. Friday night’s opening show was to be headlined by John Mulaney, Stavros Halkias, Fred Armisen and James Austin Johnson. Saturday was to feature Adam Ray as Dr. Phil Live, Ms. J. Miller, Jeff Arcuri, Brad Williams and Grace O’Malley, while Sunday’s lineup included Matt Mathews, Jordan Jensen, Katherine Blanford, Hasan Minhaj, Ronny Chieng and Michael Kosta. The festival had been billed as a major new event for Mississauga, with organizers expecting roughly 12,500 people for each of the five shows.

items.title: Stonehooker's Lakeshore Road Restaurant Shuts Down, But Its Beer Store Stays Open
items.summary: According to INsauga, Stonehooker Brewing Co.'s Biergarten CODA restaurant, bar and hospitality operation on Lakeshore Road East closed for good on September 7. The outlet reports the closure ends the space's run as a Mississauga destination for pints, food, live music and events, though the brewery's beer store remains open. INsauga reports Stonehooker's beer also continues to be available at the LCBO, since the retail and hospitality sides of the business are separate. According to the outlet, owner Ross Noel said that distinction matters for customers who may have assumed the closure meant the end of Stonehooker altogether, noting the brand still has value. INsauga reports Stonehooker had announced the hospitality wind-down last month, and the final day included one last celebration for regulars before the doors closed.

items.title: Streetsville Loses Its BeaverTails Outlet as Shelly's Chill Also Shuts Down
items.summary: According to INsauga, the BeaverTails location at 213 Queen Street South in Streetsville has closed, along with Shelly's Chill, which operated in the same space. The outlet reports both businesses are now marked as permanently closed on Google Maps, and the BeaverTails location is no longer listed on the chain's own website. INsauga reports the Streetsville location opened in 2022, offering the chain's signature flat fried dough pastries topped with items like chocolate hazelnut spread, maple spread and crushed Oreo cookies, along with fries, poutine and ice cream. According to the outlet, BeaverTails began as a wooden booth in Ottawa's ByWard Market in 1980 and has since grown to about 50 storefronts and more than 150 mobile locations. INsauga reports Shelly's Chill, which served chicken sandwiches, bowls, shakes and fries at the same address, could not be reached for comment on the closure.

items.title: Council Revisits AI Data Centre Rules One Month Into Its Construction Moratorium
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga city officials are set to revisit the debate over large AI data centres at a general committee meeting on Wednesday, just over a month after imposing a construction moratorium on the facilities. The outlet reports a report from Planning and Building Commissioner Andrew Whittemore outlines the Ontario government's newly released playbook for building such facilities across the province. INsauga reports city council voted unanimously two weeks earlier to impose a moratorium of one to two years on data centre developments to give the city more time to study the issue. According to the outlet, that decision followed roughly two dozen deputations from residents and other stakeholders at a July 29 council meeting, with most speakers opposed to the large new facilities. INsauga reports Whittemore's report notes that significant regulatory and legislative changes would be needed to implement elements of the province's strategy.

items.title: Woman charged with attempted murder after Sunday stabbing outside Mississauga shelter
items.summary: Man rushed to hospital in critical condition. A woman has been charged with attempted murder after a man was stabbed outside a Mississauga shelter Sept. 6. A woman has been charged with attempted murder in connection with a stabbing outside a Mississauga shelter. m. Sunday, Sept. 6. He was taken to hospital in critical condition. Police said officers initially arrested a man who was involved in an altercation with the victim but he was released after police determined he wasn’t responsible for the stabbing. “Investigators identified an adult female as the stabbing suspect, who had fled the area on foot prior to police arrival,” a Sept. 7 police news release said. On Sept. 7, a 42-year-old Mississauga woman was arrested and charged and was held in custody pending a bail hearing, police said. Anyone with information regarding this incident is asked to contact investigators with the 12 Division Criminal Investigations Bureau at 905-453-2121 ext.

items.title: Showing Up Now Counts Toward Grades Under New Ontario High School Rules
items.summary: According to INsauga, a major change to how Ontario high school students are graded takes effect this year as students in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon return to class. The outlet reports the new provincial rules apply to students in Grades 9 through 12 and are being implemented by both the Peel District School Board and the Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board. INsauga reports students in Grades 9 and 10 will now have final marks calculated as 65 per cent classroom work, 20 per cent mandatory final evaluations and 15 per cent attendance and participation. According to the outlet, Grades 11 and 12 students will be graded on 65 per cent classroom work, 25 per cent final evaluations and 10 per cent attendance and participation, meaning showing up to class can now directly affect a student's mark. INsauga reports the province says excused absences, including illness, inclement weather and approved cultural or religious observances, will not count against a student's grade.

items.title: Comedy, Filipino Heritage and Literature Headline Mississauga's Sept. 11-13 Festival Weekend
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the city is hosting a busy slate of cultural festivals this September and October, including three events over the Sept. 11-13 weekend. The outlet reports those three are the 19-plus Great Outdoors Comedy Festival, featuring open-air comedy and food trucks, the Philippine Festival Mississauga, and the Mississauga Literary Festival. Mississauga.com reports the Philippine Festival is a three-day celebration hosted in partnership with Culture Philippines Ontario, held at Mississauga Celebration Square with music, dance showcases and traditional cuisine. According to the outlet, organizers expect tickets for the comedy festival to sell quickly, and the event runs rain or shine. Mississauga.com reports the Portugalo Fest is also set to return to Celebration Square on September 19.

items.title: Erin Mills Town Centre Welcomes Mississauga's First Indigenous-Owned Mall Storefront
items.summary: According to INsauga, BigCanoe Indigenous Market is opening at Erin Mills Town Centre during National Truth and Reconciliation Month, becoming the first Indigenous-owned and operated storefront in a Mississauga mall. The outlet reports the family business is owned and operated by Jared BigCanoe, a member of the Georgina Island First Nation, who aims to create a space for storytelling, ceremony, healing, art and handmade Indigenous goods. INsauga reports Jared's grandparents attended the Spanish Residential School in northern Ontario, one of the government-funded, church-run institutions that operated across Canada for over a century to forcibly separate First Nations children from their families, languages and cultures. According to the outlet, the BigCanoe family has experienced the lasting effects of that history, including loss of culture, loss of heritage and economic hardship. INsauga reports Jared said he was previously homeless and struggling with opioid addiction before building the business, which he describes as a way to continue his family's legacy.

items.title: Health inspectors temporarily shut down Mississauga restaurant
items.summary: Peel Public Health inspectors check restaurants, cocktail bars, beverage rooms, bakeries, takeout food establishments and other businesses to ensure compliance with safety standards. The Peel Public Health inspection program is designed to provide the public with information about inspections of food establishments in Peel Region. Peel Public Health officials temporarily closed a Mississauga restaurant during a recent inspection. Inspectors routinely check local restaurants, cocktail bars/beverage rooms, bakeries and takeout food establishments to ensure compliance with food safety standards. , Units 101-102, was ordered to close when it was inspected Sept. 3. According to Peel Region, inspection results were: During inspections by Peel Public Health, a green pass sign means the business establishment is following the requirements under the Health Protection and Promotion Act for food safety and operational standards for personal service settings, according to the region of Peel.

items.title: Fourteen Candidates Register for Mississauga's October Mayoral Race
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, a total of 14 candidates have registered to run for mayor of Mississauga in the city's October 26 municipal election. The outlet reports incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish, who won the seat in a 2024 byelection after decades as a city councillor and federal Liberal MP, is seeking to hold onto the position. CityNews Toronto reports polling from Liaison Strategies published August 14 suggests the race has narrowed to a head-to-head contest between Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie. According to the outlet, Crombie served a decade as Mississauga's mayor before resigning in 2024 to lead the Ontario Liberal Party, then stepped down from that role after failing to win a seat in the 2025 provincial election. CityNews Toronto reports Crombie is now looking to return to her former job in what is expected to be a high-stakes race.

items.title: Site Selection Names Mississauga a Top Canadian Investment Destination for the 10th Year Running
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, Site Selection Magazine has named Mississauga one of Canada's top-performing communities for business investment for the 10th consecutive year. The city reports the publication described Mississauga as a perennial top performer, citing its ability to attract investment, support business growth and create jobs across a diverse economy that includes advanced manufacturing, logistics, life sciences, technology and financial services. According to the city, Invest Mississauga continued its international outreach this year, including a Global Affairs Canada-led business mission to Zurich and London and engagement with life sciences and advanced manufacturing industry leaders. The city reports its entrepreneurship hub, IDEA Mississauga, helped participating companies raise more than $15 million in funding, generate $4 million in annual revenue and create 270 local jobs. According to the city, other developments behind the recognition included Council making the city's live music grant program permanent and Invest Mississauga taking on the city's film, television and music production office.
